# SEPA pain.001 Doctor: hromadné príkazy pre slovenské banky

> Free, client-side checker that finds why a SEPA pain.001 XML batch payment file (hromadný príkaz na úhradu) gets rejected by Tatra banka, Slovenská sporiteľňa (SLSP), VÚB, or ČSOB internet banking, and gives the exact bank rule it violates: instead of a bare "chyba" with no detail.

Paste your `pain.001.001.03` XML, pick the target bank, and it parses the file and cross-checks it against that specific bank's own published import requirements: every rule below is sourced from the bank's own technical documentation, not a generic ISO 20022 reading. No account, no backend, nothing you paste leaves your browser. One exception: if you choose to have the result emailed, only your email address and the finding codes with counts leave the browser, never the file.

## Why one "pain.001" isn't enough

Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, and ČSOB all say they accept "SEPA pain.001" batch imports. In practice each bank enforces a different subset of the ISO 20022 standard, with different fixed values, different limits, and different fallback behavior on the same nominal file format. A file built and tested against one bank routinely fails silently or with an unhelpful error at another: which is exactly the situation this tool targets: not "is this valid XML", but "is this valid **for this specific bank**".

## What it checks

- **Schema/namespace**: `pain.001.001.03` (root namespace `urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.03`) or `pain.001.001.09`. Any other namespace is reported, because none of the four banks lists it for batch imports. What the banks publish about the two versions, read on 19 November 2026:
  - VÚB, Internet banking guide *INTERNET BANKING Formáty importných súborov*: "Povolené sú xsd schémy pain.001.001.03 a pain.001.001.09." (both schemas are allowed). https://www.vub.sk/document/documents/VUB/IB-navody-manualy/IB-Formaty-importnych-suborov.pdf
  - ČSOB, *ISO20022 Štrukturované adresy* (1 August 2026): "Podporovaný je import XML formátu verzie pain.001.001.03 aj pain.001.001.09" and "ČSOB bude naďalej podporovať formát pain.001.001.03." (the answer for files without addresses; elsewhere the bank adds "za predpokladu správneho vyplnenia adries", i.e. provided addresses are filled in correctly). https://www.csob.sk/documents/11005/100040/ISO20022_Strukturovane_adresy.pdf
  - Slovenská sporiteľňa, Business24 page, "Popis štruktúr pre import úhrad": CGI specifications for both `pain.001.001.03` and `pain.001.001.09` (content dated 14 September 2026), no end date for `.03`. https://www.slsp.sk/sk/biznis/elektronicke-bankovnictvo/business24
  - Tatra banka, Internet bankingTB batch files page: `Pain.001.09` samples and a table of `.09` restrictions, plus the older `pain.001.03` description. An April 2026 version of the Slovak page announced `.03` imports only until 12 November 2026; the English page read on 19 November 2026 does not give that date. Whether Tatra banka still accepts `.03` after that date is not verified. https://www.tatrabanka.sk/en/personal/account-payments/internet-banking/batch-files/
  A `pain.001.001.09` file is therefore not a finding for these four banks; with "another bank" it gets a low-severity note to check that bank's documentation.
- **Fixed field values**: `PmtMtd` must be `TRF`; `InstrPrty` must be `NORM` (VÚB explicitly allows `HIGH` too, but then processes the payment as an urgent, fee-bearing transfer instead of standard SEPA); `PmtTpInf/SvcLvl/Cd` must be `SEPA`; `ChrgBr` must be `SLEV`. VÚB's spec adds that asserting `SvcLvl/Cd = SEPA` on a payment that doesn't actually meet SEPA's conditions gets it rejected and excluded from processing rather than silently downgraded to a cross-border transfer.
- **`ReqdExctnDt` window, bank-specific**: must not be in the past, and:
  - Tatra banka: rejects a date more than **31 days** ahead ([*Prenosový formát pain.001.001.03 v štruktúre XML*](https://www.tatrabanka.sk/files/sk/personal/ucet-platby/elektronicke-bankovnictvo/internet-banking/davkove-platby/prenosovy_formatpain001.pdf), section 1.2, element `ReqdExctnDt`: "Nesmie byť spätný dátum a dopredný dátum viac ako 31 dní").
  - VÚB: accepts a requested execution/booking date of **max +30 days** ahead ([*Popis formátu pre SEPA úhrady - SCT*](https://app.vub.sk/source/files/vubweb/sekundarna-navigacia/informacny-servis/sepa-aplikacie/sct_klient_f.pdf): "VÚB akceptuje platby s požadovaným dátumom zaúčtovania platby max +30 dní vopred").
  - The date also must be identical for every payment inside one `PmtInf` block (Tatra banka's spec).
- **Transaction count**: Tatra banka's spec (page 3, row 2.0 `PmtInf`) says "Max. 500 transakcií v súbore": at most **500 transactions in the whole file**, counted across all `PmtInf` blocks. Two blocks of 300 are over the limit. A file with more transactions isn't truncated: it's rejected.
- **Tatra banka and `pain.001.001.09`**: the bank's Internet bankingTB batch files page (read on 19 November 2026) has a table "Differences and other restrictions for Pain.001.09 compared to SEPA definitions". The element numbers follow the EPC SCT Customer-to-PSP Implementation Guidelines the bank links to. For a `.09` file with Tatra banka selected, the Doctor reports four of them as medium-severity warnings, because the bank lists the restriction but does not say what it does with a file that breaks it: more than one `PmtInf` block (2.0, "Maximum 1 element"), `BtchBookg` = `true` (2.3, "Batch booking is not supported"), a hybrid creditor address, `AdrLine` together with structured fields in `Cdtr/PstlAdr` (2.118, "Use of hybrid address is not supported"), and `RmtInf/Strd` (2.166, "RemittanceInformation/Structured is not supported"). The `InitgPty/Nm` pattern from the bank's `.03` description is not applied to `.09` files. https://www.tatrabanka.sk/en/personal/account-payments/internet-banking/batch-files/
- **Debtor bank identity**: the file's `DbtrAgt/FinInstnId/BIC` has to be the selected bank's own BIC: Tatra banka only accepts `TATRSKBX` there ("Musí byť iba 'TATRSKBX'"), VÚB's is `SUBASKBX`. A file whose debtor account is actually held at a different bank, imported into the wrong bank's internet banking, is a common copy-paste mistake when a company holds accounts at more than one bank.
- **Creditor BIC handling: genuinely different per bank:**
  - Tatra banka: `CdtrAgt/BIC` can be omitted if the creditor IBAN is valid and belongs to a SEPA-space bank (the BIC is derived from the IBAN); if a BIC is supplied anyway, its first 6 characters must match the derived one, and if the derived BIC isn't in SEPA space at all, the payment is rejected outright.
  - VÚB: `Creditor Agent BIC (AT23)` is listed as **Mandatory** in VÚB's own field table: omitting it is not tolerated the way Tatra banka tolerates it.
  - ČSOB: BIC of the creditor's bank became **optional** for SEPA payments from **1 February 2016** ([*BusinessBanking Lite a SEPA*](https://www.csob.sk/documents/11005/123723/BB_SEPA_01022016.pdf)).
  A file that omits creditor BIC because it worked fine at Tatra banka or ČSOB will get rejected at VÚB for that reason alone.
- **Character set / diacritics**: ČSOB documents, in plain terms, that a SEPA XML file containing diacritics **cannot be imported** into BusinessBanking Lite, and publishes the allowed set explicitly: `a-z A-Z 0-9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' +`. Any "š", "č", "ž", "ä", "ô", "ľ" etc. in a debtor/creditor name, address line, or remittance text: trivial to leave in when the value comes straight out of an accounting system's customer database: breaks the import. This is stricter than the base ISO 20022 SEPA character set most other documents only describe informally.
- **Field length limits**: Debtor/creditor `Nm` capped at **70 characters** (Tatra banka, VÚB); unstructured remittance info `RmtInf/Ustrd` capped at **140 characters**, and **only one `Ustrd` instance** is allowed per transaction (EPC: "Only one occurrence of 'Unstructured' is allowed"); Tatra banka's `.03` format description adds that the extra elements are removed ("Povolená je iba jedna inštancia Ustrd. Nadbytočné elementy budú odstránené.").
- **Unstructured or structured remittance, not both (added 25 November 2026)**: the EPC SCT Customer-to-PSP Implementation Guidelines, EPC132-08 2021 Version 1.0 for `pain.001.001.03` (elements 2.137 to 2.145) and 2025 Version 1.0 for `pain.001.001.09` (elements 2.164 to 2.175), say for `RmtInf` "Either 'Structured' or 'Unstructured' may be present", for `Strd` "Only one occurrence of 'Structured' is allowed" and "'Structured' can be used, provided the tags and the data within the 'Structured' element (i.e. excluding <Strd> and </Strd>) do not exceed 140 characters in length", and for `CdtrRefInf` "When used both 'Type' and 'Reference' must be present" with "Only 'SCOR' is allowed" as the type code. The ISO 20022 schema allows `Ustrd` and `Strd` any number of times, so a schema-valid file can still break these rules, and an import that only validates the schema reports nothing. The Slovak SBA standard for `pain.001` (CGI, `.03` version 1.0 and `.09`, published inside the import specifications of Slovenská sporiteľňa and ČSOB) allows only `Strd` or `Ustrd` for a SEPA credit transfer and one `Strd` of at most 140 characters (counted there without tag names). Bank documents: in the validation column of Slovenská sporiteľňa's `.09` specification (requirement REQ-20584, shared by about 20 checks) "IF Strd and Ustrd are used both then REASON:FF01", and for `CdtrRefInf` "REASON:RR09 ... When used both Creditor Reference Type and Creditor Reference must be present" (when the type code is filled in and `Ref` is empty); FF01 is also used there for other checks, such as the creditor address. VÚB writes "VÚB pre SEPA úhrady bude používať výhradne USTRD formu"; Tatra banka's `.03` description says "Vyplnený je element Ustrd alebo Strd." No source says which element takes precedence when both are present. The Doctor reports `rmt_inf_ustrd_and_strd` (high for Slovenská sporiteľňa and `.09`, otherwise medium), `rmt_inf_multiple_strd` (medium), `rmt_inf_strd_too_long` (medium, the length counts the tags and data inside `Strd`, whitespace between tags excluded) and `rmt_inf_creditor_ref_incomplete` (high for Slovenská sporiteľňa and `.09` when a type code has no `Ref`, otherwise low, as EPC says the payer's bank is not obliged to validate the reference; a type in `Prtry` is reported too, the SBA standard does not support it for SEPA). A payment tagged `PERI` in `LclInstrm/Cd` uses the optional EPC Extended Remittance Information service (Annex V of the SCT rulebook): one `Ustrd`, up to 999 `Strd` of up to 280 characters each, only between banks that adhere to it. The Doctor applies that exception only when no bank is selected: Slovenská sporiteľňa lists `LclInstrm` only for instant payments and says "Iné hodnoty ako uvedené budú vyhodnotené ako nepoužitie tagu LclInstrm", and VÚB, ČSOB and Tatra banka do not mention `PERI` in their import documentation. When every `Strd` holds nothing but `CdtrRefInf/Ref` made of Slovak payment symbols (`VS:202611`, `KS:0138`, `/VS1/SS2/KS3`) and the beneficiary account is Slovak (SK IBAN), the suggested fix shows them in `EndToEndId` as `/VS202611/SS/KS0138` (SBA standard within Slovakia: "/VS(10)/SS(10)/KS(4)"; outside Slovakia SBA does not allow `/` as the first character; VÚB's example `/VS123/SS456/KS0308`; ČSOB writes empty symbols as `/VS123/SS/KS`), keeps the text in `Ustrd` and drops `Strd`, with XML comments that say where each part goes. If `EndToEndId` already holds the same symbols (compared as numbers, also with the `?/` prefix some Slovak banks use since 18 March 2024), only `Strd` is dropped; if it holds some of them, the missing ones are added; if it holds different ones, if `Strd` holds anything else (an RF reference, an invoice number in `RfrdDocInf`) or if the beneficiary account is not Slovak, no value is suggested, so nothing is dropped silently. Sources: https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/kb/file/2020-11/EPC132-08%20SCT%20C2PSP%20IG%202021%20V1.0.pdf, https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/sites/default/files/kb/file/2025-10/EPC132-08%20SCT%20C2PSP%20IG%202025%20V1.0.pdf, https://cdn.erstegroup.com/content/dam/sk/slsp/www_slsp_sk/documents/Zip/xml-platby-cgi-pain-001-001-09.zip, https://www.csob.sk/documents/11005/100040/CSOB_SK_PAIN_001_001_09_MCCv3, https://app.vub.sk/source/files/vubweb/sekundarna-navigacia/informacny-servis/sepa-aplikacie/sct_klient_f.pdf, https://www.tatrabanka.sk/files/sk/personal/ucet-platby/elektronicke-bankovnictvo/internet-banking/davkove-platby/prenosovy_formatpain001.pdf.
- **VS/špecifický symbol/KS (Slovak payment reference symbols)**: `pain.001.001.03` has no dedicated fields for these. They must be packed into the end-to-end reference following the National Bank of Slovakia convention, in exact order: `/VS.../SS.../KS...`. ČSOB's own guide gives worked examples of the wrong order (`/VS123/KS0308/SS14` instead of `/VS123/SS14/KS0308`) breaking automatic reconciliation on the counterparty's side even though the transfer itself succeeds: the payment goes through, but nobody can match it to an invoice.
- **Slashes in references and identifiers (EPC rule)**: the EPC SEPA Credit Transfer Customer-to-PSP Implementation Guidelines (EPC132-08, 2025 Version 1.0, section 1.4 "Character Set") say that for references, identifications and identifiers "Content must not start or end with a '/'" and "Content must not contain '//'s". The EPC clarification paper EPC230-15 lists the affected `pain.001` elements, the same for `pain.001.001.03` (v1.0) and `pain.001.001.09` (v2.0): `MsgId`, `PmtInfId`, `InstrId`, `EndToEndId`, and `Id/OrgId/Othr/Id` and `Id/PrvtId/Othr/Id` of the initiating party, debtor, ultimate debtor, creditor and ultimate creditor. The Doctor reports each such value as a medium-severity finding (a warning, not a blocking error) with a corrected value to copy, for example `0000000099//2026-11-12/BO-1` becomes `0000000099/2026-11-12/BO-1`. Not covered: `RmtInf/Strd/CdtrRefInf/Ref` and `DbtrAgt/FinInstnId/Othr/Id` are explicitly excluded in EPC230-15, and `RmtInf/Ustrd` is not in its list at all. One deliberate exception: an `EndToEndId` that starts with the Slovak `/VS`, `/SS` or `/KS` symbol convention is not reported for its leading slash, because Slovak banks prescribe that convention themselves; `//` and a trailing slash are still reported there, and the corrected value keeps one leading slash (`//VS123` becomes `/VS123`). Whether a particular Slovak bank rejects such a value on import is not something we have verified, which is why the severity is medium and not high. When that exception applies, the message says that the leading slash is a Slovak convention; the suggested value keeps the 35-character limit of `MsgId` and `EndToEndId`, and when the symbols are also in the wrong order it already uses the canonical order: `/SS456//VS123/KS0308` becomes `/VS123/SS456/KS0308`. When the value holds more than the symbols, the other text is kept after them (`/SS1//VS2/KS3/FA2026-001` becomes `/VS2/SS1/KS3/FA2026-001`), so the suggested value passes both checks; the order finding then carries no second, identical suggestion.
- **Slovak creditor IBAN: a second, domestic checksum on top of MOD-97**: for a creditor IBAN issued by a Slovak bank, Tatra banka's spec additionally validates the last 10 digits of the BBAN against Slovakia's **modulo-11** algorithm. A structurally valid IBAN (correct international MOD-97 check digits) can still fail this bank-specific second check.
- **Instant-payment flag at SLSP**: Slovenská sporiteľňa's Business24 only treats a payment as instant when `PmtTpInf/LclInstrm/Cd` is set to `INST`, either at the file/group header level or per individual payment. An export that doesn't set it is processed as a normal (non-instant) SEPA transfer with no error: the file "succeeds" but not the way the payroll run intended.

## Who it's for

Slovak and Czech accountants, ERP/e-shop developers, and business owners whose accounting software (Pohoda, Money S3, KROS Omega, or a custom in-house export) produces a `pain.001` batch payment file that Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, or ČSOB internet banking rejects: with an error message that names an error code but not which element or value caused it.

## How it works

Static HTML plus one dependency-free JavaScript file, `doctor-pain001.js`. The page parses the XML you paste and runs the checks above entirely client-side. There is no backend, no upload, and no request that carries your payment data anywhere: read `index.html` and `doctor-pain001.js` directly to verify. One exception: if you choose to have the result emailed, only your email address and the finding codes with counts leave the browser, never the file.

## Free check, paid options

The check is free, with no account and no limit on the number of checks. Two paid options exist:

- **Automatic fix, 29 EUR per file, VAT included.** When the check finds problems the tool can repair (unstructured addresses split into fields, country names turned into codes, IBANs without spaces, recalculated control totals), the page shows a preview and offers the corrected XML. The fix runs in the browser; the file is never sent to ARLing. Paid by card through Stripe Managed Payments, where Link (Sold through Link, LLC) is the merchant of record and sends the receipt and the invoice. The corrected file can be downloaded for 24 hours after payment. If it does not download or is fixed wrongly, support@arling.sk fixes it by hand or refunds.
- **SEPA file check by a person, 149 EUR, once, no subscription.** Ordered through the form at https://arling.sk/kontrola-suboru/en/; within 24 hours of receiving the file ARLing s. r. o. sends the corrected file and a written report. Nothing is paid upfront and Stripe is not used: ARLing s. r. o. issues the invoice only after delivery, payable by bank transfer. If the file is not delivered within 24 hours or cannot be fixed, there is no invoice.

Terms: https://arling.sk/podmienky/en/ (section 7). Neither option guarantees that the bank accepts the file.

## Worked example

Input: a batch file exported by an accounting package for import into **ČSOB**, targeting a Tatra banka business account, where the creditor name still has its original diacritics and the VS/KS order is swapped in the reference:

```xml
<Document xmlns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:pain.001.001.03">
  <CstmrCdtTrfInitn>
    <GrpHdr>
      <MsgId>FA2026-0912</MsgId>
      <CreDtTm>2026-09-04T09:00:00</CreDtTm>
      <NbOfTxs>1</NbOfTxs>
    </GrpHdr>
    <PmtInf>
      <PmtInfId>FA2026-0912-1</PmtInfId>
      <PmtMtd>TRF</PmtMtd>
      <PmtTpInf><SvcLvl><Cd>SEPA</Cd></SvcLvl></PmtTpInf>
      <ReqdExctnDt>2026-09-04</ReqdExctnDt>
      <Dbtr><Nm>Firma s.r.o.</Nm></Dbtr>
      <DbtrAcct><Id><IBAN>SK8911000000002619174231</IBAN></Id></DbtrAcct>
      <DbtrAgt><FinInstnId><BIC>TATRSKBX</BIC></FinInstnId></DbtrAgt>
      <ChrgBr>SLEV</ChrgBr>
      <CdtTrfTxInf>
        <PmtId><EndToEndId>/VS123/KS0308/SS14</EndToEndId></PmtId>
        <Amt><InstdAmt Ccy="EUR">450.00</InstdAmt></Amt>
        <Cdtr><Nm>Jozef Šťastný</Nm></Cdtr>
        <CdtrAcct><Id><IBAN>SK6807200002891987426353</IBAN></Id></CdtrAcct>
        <RmtInf><Ustrd>Faktúra č. 2026-0912</Ustrd></RmtInf>
      </CdtTrfTxInf>
    </PmtInf>
  </CstmrCdtTrfInitn>
</Document>
```

Output:

```json
{
  "status": "fail",
  "bank": "csob",
  "summary": "3 issues found. Most urgent: the creditor name \"Jozef Šťastný\" and the remittance text both contain diacritics: ČSOB documents that a SEPA XML file with diacritics cannot be imported into BusinessBanking Lite at all.",
  "problems": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "code": "diacritics_in_field",
      "message": "\"Jozef Šťastný\" (Cdtr/Nm) contains characters outside ČSOB's documented SEPA XML character set (a-z A-Z 0-9 / - ? : ( ) . , ' +). ČSOB states this file type cannot be imported with diacritics present.",
      "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/Cdtr/Nm"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "code": "diacritics_in_field",
      "message": "\"Faktúra č. 2026-0912\" (RmtInf/Ustrd) contains diacritics: same restriction as above.",
      "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/RmtInf/Ustrd"
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "code": "reference_symbol_order",
      "message": "EndToEndId \"/VS123/KS0308/SS14\" packs the Slovak payment symbols out of order. The NBS convention is /VS/SS/KS: this should read \"/VS123/SS14/KS0308\". The transfer will still go through, but the counterparty's accounting software likely won't auto-match it to an invoice.",
      "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/PmtId/EndToEndId"
    }
  ],
  "fixes": [
    { "title": "Replace diacritics with plain Latin equivalents", "value": "Jozef Stastny", "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/Cdtr/Nm" },
    { "title": "Replace diacritics with plain Latin equivalents", "value": "Faktura c. 2026-0912", "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/RmtInf/Ustrd" },
    { "title": "Reorder to /VS/SS/KS", "value": "/VS123/SS14/KS0308", "where": "CdtTrfTxInf/PmtId/EndToEndId" }
  ],
  "checklist": [
    "Fix your accounting software's export step (or add a transliteration pass) so it never emits diacritics into a SEPA XML file for ČSOB.",
    "Standardize VS/SS/KS packing in one place in your export pipeline so the order never has to be fixed by hand again.",
    "Re-run this check after every accounting-software update: export templates for hromadné príkazy change without much notice."
  ]
}
```

Everything else in this file is fine for ČSOB specifically: `PmtMtd`, `SvcLvl/Cd`, `ChrgBr`, the IBANs, and the execution date are all valid. Note that the debtor's own bank BIC here is `TATRSKBX` (Tatra banka): that's fine as far as pain.001 structure goes (it's just naming which bank holds the debit account), but if this file were instead being imported into Tatra banka's own internet banking rather than ČSOB's, the tool's "reference symbols" and diacritics checks are ČSOB-specific advisories in this example and wouldn't change; what would change is that Tatra banka additionally caps the file at 500 transactions and its own ±31-day execution-date window, and ChrgBr/PmtMtd/SvcLvl requirements it shares with the other banks would apply identically.

## FAQ

**Why does my accounting software's SEPA export get rejected by one bank but not another, even though both say they accept "pain.001"?**
Because "pain.001" names the XML schema, not the bank's full acceptance rules. Tatra banka, SLSP, VÚB, and ČSOB each layer their own fixed-value requirements, length limits, and execution-date windows on top of the same schema, and none of it is visible from the file being schema-valid: a file can validate against the pain.001.001.03 XSD and still get bounced by a specific bank's business rules.

**My bank's import screen just says "chyba" / gives an error code with no explanation. Where do I even start?**
Start with the checks that fail silently rather than loudly: diacritics anywhere in the XML (ČSOB), a missing or mismatched creditor BIC (VÚB requires it, Tatra banka often doesn't), and the execution-date window (31 days at Tatra banka, 30 at VÚB). These four cover most "the XML looks fine to me" rejections reported by Slovak accounting-software users.

**Do I need to include the creditor's BIC code?**
Depends which bank. VÚB's own spec marks it mandatory. Tatra banka accepts a valid SEPA creditor IBAN without one (it derives the BIC itself, and only rejects if the derived BIC isn't in SEPA space or doesn't match one you did supply). ČSOB made it optional for all SEPA payments from 1 February 2016. If you generate one file for import at multiple banks, include it: it's accepted everywhere it isn't required.

**Why did my payment go through but the counterparty can't match it to an invoice?**
Almost always the VS/špecifický symbol/KS packing in the end-to-end reference. `pain.001.001.03` has no dedicated fields for these Slovak payment symbols: they have to be encoded as `/VS.../SS.../KS...`, in exactly that order. Get the order wrong (or omit a symbol without leaving its slot empty, e.g. `/VS123` instead of `/VS123/SS/KS`) and the transfer completes normally while automatic reconciliation on the other end silently fails.

**Why does my file work one week and get rejected the next with the same content?**
Check the requested execution date against today's date, not the date you actually generate the file. Both Tatra banka (31 days) and VÚB (30 days) enforce a rolling window from the day the bank processes the file, not from when your accounting software built it: a file that sat in an approval queue for a few days can drift past the limit.

**Does this tool submit or verify anything against my actual bank account?**
No. It's a read-only, client-side structural check against each bank's published rules: it has no connection to any bank, doesn't call any API, and can't tell you whether your account has sufficient funds, whether the creditor account actually exists, or anything else that depends on live banking infrastructure.

**What about Slovenská sporiteľňa (SLSP): the checks look thinner than for the other three banks.**
SLSP's own detailed pain.001 field-level specification isn't published the way Tatra banka's, VÚB's, and ČSOB's are (SLSP's public documentation covers its proprietary Databanking/Internet Banking XML interface in more detail than its pain.001 import). The checks this tool applies for SLSP are the ones confirmed from SLSP's own public statements: Business24 accepts `pain.001.001.003` and `pain.001.001.004`, validates against an XSD, and requires `PmtTpInf/LclInstrm/Cd = INST` for a batch to be routed as an instant payment. If you hit an SLSP-specific rejection this tool doesn't explain, please open an issue: see the README.

## Privacy

No account, no login, no cookies for the tool itself, no server-side processing of your payment file. The only analytics are anonymous usage counts (event name + count, never IBANs, names, or amounts) sent to a self-hosted Umami instance.
